chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who fell ill in Ramadan and died in Shawwal, and she instructed me to make up the fasts on her behalf. He said: 'Did she recover from her illness?' I said: 'No, she died while still ill.' He said: 'Then do not make up the fasts on her behalf, for Allah did not impose it upon her.' I said: 'But I wish to make up the fasts on her behalf, and she had instructed me to do so.' He said: 'How can you make up for something that Allah did not impose upon her? If you wish to fast for your own sake, then fast.'

key_terms.لَمْ يَجْعَلْهُ عَلَيْهَا: Did not impose it upon her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up the fasts of a person who died while still ill in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that if a woman dies in Shawwal having been ill throughout Ramadan without recovering, her obligatory make-up fasts (qada) are not due, as the illness exempted her and death finalized that exemption. This ruling highlights the Shia principle that the obligation to make up fasts is contingent upon survival and recovery; thus, one may voluntarily fast on her behalf, but it is not a mandatory debt of the deceased. This distinction underscores the mercy in divine law, where the burden of worship is lifted by illness is not reinstated by death.
